rows.note: Use this as the everyday all-purpose noun for someone highly skilled at a subject or activity.

example.english: I know a master at video games.
example.jyutping: ngo5 sik1 dak1 jat1 go3 daa2 gei1 gou1 sau2

rows.note: Use this for the owner of an animal, or historically for a person who owns or controls a slave.

example.english: The master of this dog lives next door.
example.traditional: 呢隻狗嘅主人住喺隔籬。
example.jyutping: ni1 zek3 gau2 ge3 zyu2 jan4 zyu6 hai2 gaak3 lei4

rows.note: Use this colloquial term for the person in charge who makes the decisions, rather than for an owner or an expert.

example.english: The master in charge says this shop will be closed tomorrow.
example.traditional: 呢間舖頭個話事人話聽日唔開門。
example.jyutping: ni1 gaan1 pou3 tau4 go3 waa6 si6 jan4 waa6 ting1 jat6 m4 hoi1 mun4

rows.note: Use this for the physical original of a document; a recording usually needs a more specialized term.

example.english: This is the master copy of the contract, so keep it safe.
example.traditional: 呢份係份合約嘅原件，你收好。
example.jyutping: ni1 fan6 hai6 fan6 hap6 joek3 ge3 jyun4 gin6 nei5 sau1 hou2
